subject: Handoff: model fit recommendations & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@lightrx.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lightrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: model fit recommendations & evaluation plan

Hi Emily / Daniel —

Thanks again for today’s demo and for walking us through the patient-summary flow. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we have alignment internally and externally: 

Summary of needs (what we heard)
- Short clinical summaries from structured EHR + free-text notes (~3–5 sentences)
- High precision on facts (no hallucinations), conservative paraphrasing
- Low latency requirement for UI: <400ms median token latency

Initial recommendations
- Model family: prefer open LLM variants with safety-tuned instruction heads. We recommend trying redwood/gpt-instruct-3b-q4 (baseline) and redwood/gpt-instruct-7b-q4f16 for higher fidelity.
- Pin strategy: run a short canary on the 3b variant, pin to 3b for critical patient flows and keep 7b as a secondary for batch re-runs.

Deliverables we’ll share by Monday:
- Eval pack with 120 prompt+reference pairs (attached as eval-pack-v2.zip)
- Canonical prompt set for patient-summary (prompt-sets/patient-summary-v1.json)
- Benchmarks: latency, per-token cost estimate, and quality percentiles for both variants (links below).

Asks for LighthouseRx
- Provide a small sample of 200 real prompts (anonymized) or a synthetic set we can use for a closed eval run.
- Confirm any additional regulatory constraints (retention, redaction) so we can scope private deployment if needed.

Next steps
1) Emily: share sample prompts or confirm synthetic generation by Tue 10/13.
2) Redwood: run evals, share scoreboard + diff report.
3) Set up a short canary (48–72h) once you approve the pin plan.

I’ve looped in Ben (SE) to outline the eval plan and Marissa on commercial / timeline. Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: eval-pack-v2.zip, prompt-sets/patient-summary-v1.json
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@lightrx.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lightrx.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: model fit recommendations & evaluation plan

Hi Emily / Daniel —

Following Rafael’s note, I ran a quick dry eval against the 120-case pack that Rafael attached. Quick technical notes and recommended configuration: 

What I tested
- redwood/gpt-instruct-3b-q4 (q4 quantized float path)
- redwood/gpt-instruct-7b-q4f16 (higher capacity, f16 kernels)
- Prompt template: patient-summary-v1 (attached) with max_tokens=150 and temperature=0.0 for determinism.

Findings (short)
- 3b-q4: median latency 320ms (p50 token), cost est $0.0028 per prompt, factual precision 92% on our reference set. Very good for interactive UI.
- 7b-q4f16: median latency 610ms, cost est $0.0066 per prompt, precision 96% (better entity handling in notes with longer context).
- Failure modes: both models sometimes drop medication dosages when notes use shorthand; prompt engineering mitigates ~70% of those cases.

Links / artifacts
- Eval run: https://redwood.app/evals/DL-45871/pack-v2 (full scoreboard + per-example diffs)
- Prompt set (canonical): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/prompt-sets/patient-summary-v1.json

Recommended plan
- Canary: Pin redwood/gpt-instruct-3b-q4 for UI endpoints for 72 hours (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%) with auto-rollout on no-regression policy.
- Batch reprocessing: use 7b-q4f16 nightly for longer context, where latency is less critical.
- Pin/versioning: If you see quality regress, we can pin to a specific model digest (e.g., model:3b-q4@sha256:abcd1234) and block rolling updates until regression triage completes.

Immediate mitigations for reported hallucinations (if you see them)
- Set temperature=0.0 and enable conservative decoding (top_k=40).
- Add guardrail step: post-process to verify entity presence against notes (we can provide a microservice if helpful).

I’ve attached the eval pack and the prompt set we used. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk the scoreboard.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: eval-pack-v2.zip, prompt-sets/patient-summary-v1.json
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@lightrx.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lightrx.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: model fit recommendations & evaluation plan

Hi Rafael / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the eval pack. We spun up the 3b canary overnight and are seeing an uptick in hallucinations on a subset of our cardiac notes. Examples below (sanitized):

Example 1
Input: "Pt c/o CP x2d, no prior MI, troponin neg, no aspirin"
Expected: "No evidence of myocardial infarction; troponin negative. No aspirin currently prescribed."
Observed (3b-q4): "Patient reports chest pain consistent with prior MI; troponin elevated. Start aspirin."

Example 2
Input: "Meds: lisinopril 10mg qd, metformin 500mg bid"
Expected: "Current meds include lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily."
Observed (3b-q4): "Current meds include lisinopril 20 mg and metformin 1000 mg daily."

We only flipped 5% traffic to the canary but these differences are material for clinicians. Can we either (a) rollback to the previous pinned model immediately or (b) pin to the older digest until you can triage? We need an emergency path because our compliance team flagged potential clinical-safety risk.

Also attaching a short excerpt of affected prompts (sent separately via secure upload).

Emily
Emily Torres
Product Lead, LighthouseRx
emily.torres@lightrx.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@lightrx.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lightrx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: model fit recommendations & evaluation plan

Hi Emily — thanks for the concrete examples and for flagging this promptly. We take these risks seriously. Below is an immediate mitigation plan (playbook) and timeline. We can execute rollback/pinning within the hour if you want us to.

Immediate mitigation (recommended order)
1) Temporary pin: Pin to the last-known-good digest (model:3b-q4@sha256:00ff9a7b). This is reversible and stops any further propagation of the updated weights.
2) Canary rollback: Move the canary back to 0% and re-route traffic to pinned digest.
3) Hotfix triage: Ben’s team will run a focused diff on the 20 affected examples and broader 500-case slice in parallel. Expect initial triage results in 3–4 hours.
4) Longer-term: If the regression is in the compilation/quantization path, we’ll test the same digest under the 7b runtime to isolate kernel issues; if it’s prompt-sensitivity, we’ll push a prompt-guard microservice.

Operational notes
- I’ll submit a rollback request now (ops ticket #RB-20261012-79).
- Marissa, looping you for any commercial implications and to capture a temporary SLA credit if we need to support extended triage.
- Emily: please confirm whether you want us to execute step (1) immediately or hold until Ben confirms triage approach.

Attachments: rollback-playbook.md, eval-diff-report-20261012.pdf
Links: https://redwood.app/ops/tickets/RB-20261012-79

We’ll standby for your go. Sorry for the interruption — we’ll get this stabilized quickly.

— Rafael
